name: Geochron World Clock
author: ChuckBuilds
description: High-fidelity world map clock showing the real-time day/night terminator with civil/nautical/astronomical twilight bands, the subsolar point, configurable city markers, and a digital UTC/local clock - a classic Geochron, reimagined for LED matrix panels of any size.

versions.notes: Countries stay visible on the night side at low PWM depth. At pwm_bits 7 (or a dimmed panel) night-side land and ocean rounded to the same LED step and the night side drew as one flat block. The plugin now reads the panel's pwm_bits and brightness and lifts night-side land just enough to light one step above the ocean. Panels that already showed the difference, and the emulator, draw exactly as before.

The readout is now a timezone list: your local time, then one row per city with a timezone, each a short label and the time right-aligned. Subsolar coordinates and seconds are gone from it; the local date heads it instead, and a dotted midnight line on the map shows where the date turns over. Wide panels size the sidebar to the list and page through cities that do not fit, keeping the local row pinned. Cities take an optional short label.

update_interval works. It was read and never used: the core scheduled update() at the manifest's 45 seconds whatever the setting said, because it prefers the manifest's value unless the plugin answers get_update_interval(). The plugin now returns the configured interval, so the sun position and map are recomputed at the cadence you set (15-300 s), and a web-UI change applies without a restart. Requires LEDMatrix core 3.4.0, the first with the get_update_interval() hook; the store now refuses the install on older cores (on those the setting would stay ignored).

Load the 4x6 face at 7px in the live renderer too, not only render_preview.py -- off its pixel grid the clock readout was anti-aliased. A timezone string pytz does not recognise (plugin or city) now logs a warning and falls back to the LEDMatrix timezone, then system time, instead of failing validate_config, which made core refuse to load the plugin.
Load the 4x6 face at 7px in the preview renderer -- 4x6-font is crisp only at multiples of 7.
Validation-sweep fixes; see the PR for the specific defect.

Documentation only, no behaviour change. Adds real rendered screenshots for every setting that has a visible effect and documents all 24 of them. The hero image was an uploaded GitHub attachment on an external URL; it is now a committed render that regenerates from the plugin and is verified by --check. Adds a seasonal comparison showing the terminator at both equinoxes and both solstices, rendered from the real solar code at 12:00 UTC on those dates, and a map-centring comparison for square and tall panels. Both enum settings were hash-checked: all four graticule_step_deg values and both clock_format values render distinctly. The existing content -- how it works, the aspect-ratio layout table, the default cities and the vendored-data notes -- is kept, with the cities table regaining the latitude and longitude alongside the timezone strings.

Cache the rendered map per panel size instead of holding one image and re-rendering whenever the size changes. The Vegas marquee captures this plugin at a narrower width than the panel -- 153px against 512px on the rig this was measured on -- so the single entry alternated between the two and every switch re-rendered from scratch on the render thread: 105ms recomputing a terminator that does not depend on size, plus ~150ms drawing the map, about 290ms of stalled marquee each pass. The terminator is now computed once and shared across sizes, and update() refreshes every size in use on the worker thread so the render thread finds a warm image. The clock is untouched -- it is drawn after the map on every frame, so nothing about it goes stale.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.
Add a GPL-3.0 LICENSE file (project-standard license).
